plan.melodySummary: The famous theme begins tenderly in the French Horn, migrates to Violin 1 for its lyrical expansion, then is passed to Cello and Clarinet for varied color before Violin 1 reclaims it for the triumphant high-register climax. The dynamic arc rises from an intimate !p! through espressivo swells to a full-ensemble !ff! at mm.25-28, then settles into a warm, resolved !mf! close.

sections.label: Phrase A (Statement)
sections.notes: Sing the theme !p! espressivo, gently leaning into each phrase peak with a small hairpin; linger on the half-note cadences (mm.4, 8). All other voices stay at or below !p! beneath you.

sections.label: Phrase B (Contrast)
sections.notes: Take the melody !mp! with a warm woody tone; shape the FG turns fluidly and taper into m.12. Violin 1 weaves a chromatic descending countermelody above, kept softer than the melody.

sections.label: Phrase A' (Return, grows)
sections.notes: Restate the theme !mf! with bel-canto vibrato and a broad crescendo hairpin into each phrase; use expressive portamento on the m.16 descent. Accompaniment flows in gentle arpeggios beneath, one dynamic below you.

sections.label: Phrase C (Octave lift)
sections.notes: Soar into the upper octave !f!, building through the Bm secondary-dominant color of mm.21-22 toward the sustained a4 (m.24). Horn answers with a rising countermelody kept beneath your dynamic; drive the phrase with widening hairpins.

sections.label: Climax (Tutti)
sections.notes: Full-blooded !ff! Romantic climax: attack the chordal figures (FAdf, GBeg, ceg) with ringing brilliance, all voices at maximum but the melody crowning the texture. Sustain the singing tone across the arpeggiated openings.

sections.label: Coda (Resolution)
sections.notes: Broaden !f! then diminuendo to a warm !mf!, molto espressivo; ritard slightly into the final tied d (m.32) and let the whole ensemble glow into a rich D-major resolution beneath the melody.

Violin 1.instruction: Principal lyric voice; tacet mm.1-8 to reserve entrance, then a soaring espressivo carrier with vibrato, portamento at phrase ends and expansive hairpins peaking at the mm.25-28 !ff! climax before a tender ritard into the coda.

Violin 2.instruction: Inner-voice engine: flowing broken-chord arpeggios and gently repeated eighths supplying chromatic suspensions and secondary-dominant color, always shaped one dynamic softer than the melody carrier.

Clarinet.instruction: Warm woodwind color and countermelody throughout; takes the lead !mp! espressivo at mm.9-12 with fluid turns, elsewhere adds sustained inner harmony and chromatic passing lines beneath the melody.

French Horn.instruction: Opens as the intimate !p! theme-bearer with noble singing tone and phrase-end lingering, then becomes a rising countermelody and sustained harmonic anchor, adding rhythmic weight to the tutti climax.

Cello.instruction: Foundational bass in flowing arpeggios and stepwise walking lines, doubling roots and providing expressive counter-melodic swells (mm.1-8, 29-32); keep dynamics supporting, never covering, the melody.
